messages.content: In calendar year 2025, which 10 AOs had the most regular attendance records marked FNG? Count records, exclude QSource. Columns: ao, fngs. Order count descending, then AO ascending to break ties. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: SELECT ao, count(*) AS fngs FROM posts WHERE date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND date < DATE '2026-01-01' AND is_fng GROUP BY ao ORDER BY fngs DESC, ao LIMIT 10

messages.content: Who posted together most in calendar 2025? Top 10 pairs. A workout is the same AO and date, each person counted once; exclude QSource. Put the alphabetically earlier name first in each pair. Columns: pax_1, pax_2, shared_workouts. Sort count descending, then both names ascending. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: WITH attendance AS (SELECT DISTINCT date, ao, pax FROM posts WHERE date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND date < DATE '2026-01-01') SELECT a.pax AS pax_1,b.pax AS pax_2,count(*) AS shared_workouts FROM attendance a JOIN attendance b ON a.date=b.date AND a.ao=b.ao AND a.pax<b.pax GROUP BY a.pax,b.pax ORDER BY shared_workouts DESC,pax_1,pax_2 LIMIT 10

messages.content: Who posted together most in calendar 2025? Top 10 pairs. A workout is the same AO and date, each person counted once; exclude QSource. Put the alphabetically earlier name first in each pair. Columns: pax_1, pax_2, shared_workouts. Sort count descending, then both names ascending. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

I will compare the top 10 pairs by shared AO/date workouts in calendar 2025, deduplicating attendance and excluding QSource; columns pax_1, pax_2, shared_workouts, with names alphabetical within each pair and ties sorted by both names.

Same question, but calendar 2024. Retain all counting, ordering, and column rules. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: WITH attendance AS (SELECT DISTINCT date, ao, pax FROM posts WHERE date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND date < DATE '2025-01-01') SELECT a.pax AS pax_1,b.pax AS pax_2,count(*) AS shared_workouts FROM attendance a JOIN attendance b ON a.date=b.date AND a.ao=b.ao AND a.pax<b.pax GROUP BY a.pax,b.pax ORDER BY shared_workouts DESC,pax_1,pax_2 LIMIT 10

messages.content: Between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2025 inclusive, who completed the fastest blocks of 100 regular post records? Restart numbering at 1 per PAX within this fixed period, count multiple posts per day, exclude QSource, order posts by date then AO. Compare milestones 100 to 200, 200 to 300, etc.; exclude the first-100 block. Return top 10 columns pax, from_post, to_post, start_date, end_date, elapsed_days. Sort days ascending then pax then from_post. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: WITH numbered AS (SELECT pax,date,row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY pax ORDER BY date,ao) AS n FROM posts WHERE date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND date < DATE '2026-01-01'), milestones AS (SELECT * FROM numbered WHERE n%100=0), blocks AS (SELECT pax,lag(n) OVER w AS from_post,n AS to_post,lag(date) OVER w AS start_date,date AS end_date FROM milestones WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY pax ORDER BY n)) SELECT pax,from_post,to_post,start_date,end_date,date_diff('day',start_date,end_date) AS elapsed_days FROM blocks WHERE from_post IS NOT NULL ORDER BY elapsed_days,pax,from_post LIMIT 10

messages.content: For Peacock, compare January through August inclusive in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Count regular attendance records and records marked Q; exclude QSource. Columns: year, posts, qs; year ascending. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: SELECT year(date) AS year,count(*) AS posts,count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_q) AS qs FROM posts WHERE lower(pax)='peacock' AND date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND date < DATE '2026-01-01' AND month(date)<=8 GROUP BY year ORDER BY year

messages.content: Where did Peacock post most during calendar 2025? All AOs, counting regular records, excluding QSource. Columns ao, posts; count descending then AO ascending. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: SELECT ao,count(*) AS posts FROM posts WHERE lower(pax)='peacock' AND date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY ao ORDER BY posts DESC,ao

messages.content: Show monthly South Fork attendance in calendar 2024 to explore seasonality. Deduplicate person/AO/date for attendance; distinct AO/date identifies a workout. Exclude QSource. Columns month (integer 1–12), posts, workouts, unique_pax; month ascending. Return the query table using exactly the requested columns in that order; no extra rank or percentage columns. Explain it briefly.

sql: WITH attendance AS (SELECT DISTINCT date,ao,pax FROM posts WHERE date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND date < DATE '2025-01-01') SELECT month(date) AS month,count(*) AS posts,count(DISTINCT (date,ao)) AS workouts,count(DISTINCT pax) AS unique_pax FROM attendance GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

messages.content: Which 10 PAX had most regular attendance records marked Q in calendar 2023, excluding QSource? Columns pax, qs. Sort qs descending then pax ascending. sql: SELECT pax,count(*) AS qs FROM posts WHERE is_q AND date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND date < DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY pax ORDER BY qs DESC,pax LIMIT 10
